etymology: From Proto-Germanic *ahô, of uncertain origin; some have connected it to Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ- (“to see”), which however has significant phonological and semantic difficulties.
From 𐌰𐌽𐌳𐌰- (anda-) + *𐍅𐌹𐌶𐌽𐍃 (*wizns), of uncertain origin; possibly related to 𐍅𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽 (wisan, “to be, remain”) and/or 𐍅𐌹𐌶𐍉𐌽 (wizōn, “to lead a life”).
From 𐌰𐌽𐌳𐌰- (anda-) + *𐍅𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌶𐌽 (*wleizn), of uncertain origin. Perhaps related to 𐍅𐌻𐌹𐍄𐍃 (wlits).

gloss: both (referring to each of two items or of two sets of items)
etymology: From or closely related to 𐌱𐌰𐌹 (bai), from Proto-Germanic *bai. The last element is of disputed origin; it may possibly be from a neuter dual or plural *bajō followed by a form of Proto-Germanic *sa; thus, it would resemble the formation of Old Norse báðir. A derivation with the suffix of 𐌼𐌴𐌽𐍉𐌸𐍃 (mēnōþs) is also formally possible, but is judged less likely by Lehmann (1986).
From 𐌿𐌽- (un-) + a word related to 𐌰𐌽𐌳𐍃𐌰𐌺𐌰𐌽 (andsakan, “to dispute”) of uncertain derivation.
Unknown; no clear etymology and no cognates. It has been suggested to derive from 𐍃𐍅𐌰𐍂𐌰𐌽 (swaran, “to swear an oath”) + -𐌴 (-ē, adverbial suffix), although this is semantically difficult.
From Proto-Germanic *frastiz, of uncertain origin.
From the same root as 𐌰𐌷𐌰 (aha), which is of uncertain origin. The suffix represents Proto-Germanic *-mô, which derives from Proto-Indo-European *-mō.
From Proto-Germanic *bauþaz, *baudaz (“dull, deaf”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew- (“to strike”).
From 𐌲𐌰- (ga-) + *𐌸𐌻𐌰𐌹𐌷𐌰𐌽 (*þlaihan), of uncertain origin.
From 𐌲𐌰- (ga-) + *𐍅𐌹𐌶𐌽𐍃 (*wizns) (of uncertain origin; possibly related to 𐍅𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽 (wisan, “to be, remain”) or 𐍅𐌹𐌶𐍉𐌽 (wizōn, “to lead a life”)) + -𐌴𐌹𐌲𐍃 (-eigs).

gloss: Verbal prefix indicating movement towards, or arrival/presence at, something or -place.
etymology: The preposition 𐌳𐌿 (du) used as a prefix, of uncertain origin.
Apparently from *hulą, with a suffix of unclear origin or meaning.
From 𐌹𐌽- (in-) + a Germanic root of uncertain etymology, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *krewh₂- (“blood”) and thus related to 𐌷𐍂𐌰𐌹𐍅𐌰𐌳𐌿𐌱𐍉 (hraiwadubō, “turtledove”, literally “corpse dove”).
From Proto-Germanic *mōtō (“tax, toll”), of uncertain origin.
From 𐌿𐌽- (un-) + *𐌼𐌰𐌽𐌰𐍂𐌹𐌲𐌲𐍅𐍃 (*manariggws, “tamed”), from the combining form of 𐌼𐌰𐌽𐌽𐌰 (manna, “human”) + *𐍂𐌹𐌲𐌲𐍅𐍃 (*riggws), of uncertain origin.
From 𐌿𐌽- (un-) + *𐍃𐌿𐍄𐌹 (*suti). The latter element is of unclear origin.

gloss: cane (plant with a simple and flexible stem, or the stem thereof)
etymology: From Proto-Germanic *rauzą, of obscure origin. Cognate to Old High German rôr (whence German German Rohr) and close in formation to Old Norse reyrr (“reed”). Compare also English rush, which may be related.

gloss: twig or branch of a bush
etymology: From Proto-Germanic *tainaz of uncertain etymology. Cognate to Old Norse teinn (“twig, sprout”) and Old Saxon tēn (“staff”), among others.
From 𐍆𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌰 (faura) + *𐍄𐌰𐌽𐌹 (*tani). Second element is of unclear origin.
